chunks: 5835 - Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿUmayr narrated from Abān ibn ʿUthmān, Hishām ibn Sālim, and Muḥammad ibn Ḥumrān, from al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام, who said:
“I am amazed at one who is stricken by four things—how does he not turn to four things?
I am amazed at one who is afraid—how does he not turn to His saying, Mighty and Majestic:
‘Allah is sufficient for us, and excellent is the Trustee.’
For I heard Allah, Mighty and Majestic, say immediately after it:
‘So they returned with favor from Allah and bounty; no harm touched them.’
And I am amazed at one who is distressed—how does he not turn to His saying, Exalted is He:
‘There is no god but You; glory be to You; indeed I was among the wrongdoers.’
For I heard Allah, Mighty and Majestic, say after it:
‘So We answered him and delivered him from distress, and thus do We deliver the believers.’
And I am amazed at one against whom plotting is done—how does he not turn to His saying, Exalted is He:
‘And I entrust my affair to Allah; surely Allah is Seeing of the servants.’
For I heard Allah, Mighty and Majestic, say immediately after it:
‘So Allah protected him from the evils of what they plotted.’
And I am amazed at one who desires the world and its adornment—how does he not turn to His saying, Exalted is He:
‘Whatever Allah wills; there is no power except through Allah.’
For I heard Allah, Mighty and Majestic, say after it: ‘If you see me less than you in wealth and children, then perhaps my Lord will give me better than your garden’—the verse.

key_terms.الْوَكِيلُ: The trustee and disposer of affairs upon whom one relies.
key_terms.حَسْبُنَا اللَّهُ وَنِعْمَ الْوَكِيلُ: A Qur’anic declaration of trust that Allah is sufficient and the best guardian.
key_terms.سَيِّئَاتِ مَا مَكَرُوا: The harmful consequences of the plots they devised.
key_terms.لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا أَنْتَ سُبْحَانَكَ إِ: The supplication of repentance and relief associated with Prophet Yūnus عليه السلام.
key_terms.مَا شَاءَ اللَّهُ لَا قُوَّةَ إِلَّا بِا: Acknowledging that power and attainment are only by Allah’s will.
key_terms.وَأُفَوِّضُ أَمْرِي إِلَى اللَّهِ: Entrusting one’s affair fully to Allah.
key_terms.وَعَسَىٰ مُوجِبَةٌ: An affirmation that this expression indicates sure fulfillment in this context.

ai.seo_question: Which Qur’anic phrases should a believer recite in fear, distress, deception, or when seeking worldly good?
ai.summary: Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام teaches that in states of fear, grief, being plotted against, and seeking worldly good, one should turn to specific Qur’anic words of refuge and trust in Allah. The hadith links each supplication to the verse that follows it, highlighting the divine response, protection, and relief promised through these Qur’anic invocations.
